## Historical audit — S0330

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0056/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below are JSONL events; observations were supplied as whole lines, not split segments.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal and inventory | The request was to reconstruct a single RGB indoor scene with separate meshes and a matching camera. H’s inventory *interpreted* it as a cleanroom with two workers, a touchscreen, conveyor and guarded machine; hidden machinery was uncertain. These descriptions are H’s estimates, not independent image verification. (Lines 1, 3: `model_request`, `model_response`.) |
| First build | H generated named architectural, machine, screen and human assets, including screen support rods and posed limbs; it specified colored surfaces, guard opacity, lights and camera. These demonstrate modeled multiple objects, intended connections and poses—not that the parts actually connected or matched the image. Build and render completed successfully. The first projected belt endpoint was (.437, .671), versus estimated reference (.68, .94). (Lines 3–4, 6, 8–9.) |
| Review and revision | After receiving the first render, H reported small figures, missing hand-screen overlap, an upright screen and room exterior/gray surround. It moved the camera closer and inside, repositioned assets, lowered the guard and changed the figures. These are H’s visual diagnoses and executed edits, not independently checked defects or fixes. A small upward-aim trial moved projected points downward and was restored; it did **not** validate the preceding large camera relocation. Step 2 built and rendered successfully. (Lines 11, 13–14, 19.) |
| Final revision | H reported a low, round operator, small background worker, offset screen, broad belt, sparse machinery and washed-out render. It retained the camera, moved and reshaped people and screen, narrowed and shifted the belt, added dark machine elements and reduced light power. The code retained colored/transparent surfaces but no texture maps; intended material appearance is not verified. Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected. Its hairnet point projected to (.267, .106) against estimated (.32, 0); the belt point to (.784, 1.014) against (.68, .94). Point projections do not establish visible contours or occlusion. (Lines 23–24, 26, 28–30.) |

**Teacher input and autonomy:** No distinct teacher intervention is visible. The original instructions and subsequent runner prompts requested inventory, comparisons and projection checks; render images and execution results were actually supplied to H before its revisions. H’s discrepancy assessments and edits were its own observable exploration, within those prompts. Session records show no observed external tool calls by H; Blender executions were performed by the runner. (Lines 1–2, 11–13, 21–23.)

**Outcome and uncertainty:** This is a technically successful three-build/render sequence, not an empty patch or technical interruption. Final geometric and visual correctness is **unknown**: the supplied audit contains image paths, not image pixels, and no subsequent inspection of step 3 or formal quality score. Whether the final hand touches the panel, guards appear transparent, lighting is appropriate, or all reference objects are represented remains unresolved. The mismatch in selected projected points supports further investigation, not a unique camera-versus-geometry diagnosis. Transferably, distinguish execution success and point checks from image validation; task-specific changes to this cleanroom should not be generalized as proven corrections.
